utility.value: Sierra Pacific Power Company d/b/a NV Energy
utility.notes: See the identical utility-identity discussion on the Reno record (nv-washoe-reno-sierrapacific) — Sierra Pacific Power Company is the northern-Nevada NV Energy operating entity, and unincorporated Washoe County sits within its historically-documented service territory.

value.name: Sierra Pacific Power Company d/b/a NV Energy
value.notes: No Community Choice Aggregator was found serving unincorporated Washoe County this session; Sierra Pacific Power Company is recorded as both the distribution and default generation utility.

city.notes: This record covers unincorporated Washoe County only — the incorporated cities within the county (Reno, Sparks) each operate their own separate building department and are separate AHJs (see the Reno record, nv-washoe-reno-sierrapacific, for the City of Reno's own process).

permit_authority.value: Washoe County Building Department (Community Services Department, Planning & Building Division)
permit_authority.notes: Nevada has no statewide residential building code or statewide solar-permitting rule — permitting authority sits entirely with the local city or county building department. Washoe County's Building Department is the permitting authority for unincorporated areas of the county only.

interconnection_url.notes: Statewide Nevada net-metering framework (PUCN-administered). NV Energy's own utility-specific interconnection materials were inaccessible this session (see the identical notes on the Las Vegas record).

value.name: Site plan showing location of major components on the property, including arrays, energy storage, structures, and terrain features
Electrical diagram showing system configuration, wiring, overcurrent protection, and inverter details
Attachment details with rail spacing and embedment specifications
Manufacturer spec sheets and installation manuals for all components

required_documents.notes: Per the County's own Solar Photovoltaic (PV) System Permitting Checklist page. All plans must be prepared by a Nevada-licensed design professional, a licensed contractor, or an owner-builder (with affidavit).

value: One fire final inspection, scheduled before the building final inspection
A 'Qualified Person' must be present to safely access panels and make corrections during inspection

value.notes: The County's own page states it aims to complete initial reviews of complete applications within 10 business days, explicitly describing this as 'typical but not guaranteed' — delays occur when applications lack required information, contractors lack proper licensing, or equipment lacks certification.

other_conditions: Plans must be prepared by a Nevada-licensed design professional, a licensed contractor, or an owner-builder submitting an affidavit
Applications are submitted online at www.onenv.us using the 'Alternative Energy' application type
Issued permits expire 18 months after issuance

permit_fees.notes: The County's own page states fees 'vary based on contract valuation' and points to a separate fee schedule, which was not independently located and confirmed this session — left null rather than estimated.

rebates.notes: No statewide Nevada solar rebate/tax-credit program was found this session (see the identical finding on the Las Vegas record).

official_contacts.notes: No direct phone/email was extracted from the page this session; the URL itself is the County's own current contact/informational page.
